stories.title: Senate panel probes tax evasion in ex-FATA
summary: It called for the recovery of Rs85 billion for the public and sought an investigation into the role of suspended officials.
During the proceedings, officials informed the committee that the commissioner had been suspended.
The committee also expressed annoyance over the absence of the FBR chairman.

stories.title: Sanaullah calls for empowering LGs
summary: Speaking to a private television channel, he said political parties should hold discussions on the establishment of new provinces at the appropriate forum.
He said public opinion and consensus among political parties were essential for creating new provinces.
Meanwhile, Federal Minister for Climate Change Dr Musadik Malik has said that dialogue was the only way to resolve political differences and address the issues facing the country.

stories.title: 'PM must clear air on new provinces'
summary: Former prime minister Shahid Khaqan Abbasi has urged Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to publicly explain his position and the government's proposed mechanism for creating new provinces rather than leaving the issue surrounded by uncertainty.

He also launched a broadside against the government over rising inflation, administrative failures and political instability, saying the country had neither effective constitutional governance nor a coherent government policy.

Abbasi also questioned the political legitimacy of the present arrangement, saying political parties had effectively ceased to exist and that what the country had was a "Form 47 government", not a political party.

stories.title: ECP says parties control women tickets
summary: The reported directions also called on the ECP to make arrangements for filling 563 vacant seats in various local governments.

The spokesperson said the commission had already informed the parliamentary committee that, under the existing electoral framework, the allocation of party tickets to women candidates rested solely with political parties.
The ECP was neither authorised to interfere in this process nor empowered to decide which constituencies should be allocated to women candidates, the spokesperson added.

stories.title: US-Iran tensions flare over maritime blockade
summary: Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, said Tehran would neither reopen the Strait of Hormuz nor allow the American blockade to remain in place.
"Neither will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened, nor will we allow the blockade to remain in place," he said.
Also, Iranian Navy commander Rear Admiral Shahram Irani claimed that Iranian forces had struck the US aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln with a missile on the first day of the US-Israeli war.

stories.title: Hamas chief's family survives Israeli strike
summary: The son of Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya survived an Israeli airstrike targeting a residential apartment in Gaza on Friday, senior Hamas official Basem Naim said, adding that several members of the family were wounded but none killed.
In a statement, Hamas said the Israeli military had targeted a residential apartment, linking the strike to threats Defence Minister Israel Katz had made against Khalil al-Hayya.
Izzeldeen is the twin brother of Hamam Khalil al-Hayya, who was killed in an Israeli airstrike targeting Hamas leaders in Qatar in 2025, Naim said.

stories.title: Diesel tanker capsizes in Mediterranean off Ibiza
summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez told Cadena SER radio that he hoped the ship could be taken to port "in the coming hours, in the coming days".
Emergency services in the Balearic Islands, which include Ibiza, said on social media that the ship "remains stable" and tied to a rescue boat.
In 2002, Spain suffered its worst environmental disaster when the Prestige oil tanker split in two and spilled more than 60,000 tonnes of fuel, damaging thousands of kilometres of Atlantic coastline.

stories.title: Of stances and stunts
summary: Bilawal, however, was seen broadening the mosaic of political reconciliation as he once again acknowledged the PTI as a 'reality' and called for taking the party on board.
Being a component of the federation and having stakes in two provinces, as well as in Gilgit-Baltistan, Bilawal cannot just get away with knee-jerk reactions on issues of national consensus.

The JUI-F taking to the streets at a time when Islamabad is holding an international moot with allies of the Makkah Defence Pact, alongside Bilawal's maximalist position, is unnerving and ill-advised.

stories.title: Censorship as statecraft
summary: Also tellingly, the All Indian Cine Workers Association is demanding a permanent legislative ban on Pakistani artists and productions, claiming that Pakistani artists have made anti-India statements.
Those statements, it should be noted, were not necessarily anti-India, but rather pro-Pakistan.
Such censorship also does more harm to India than Pakistan.

stories.title: Cueing up greatness
summary: Pakistan's cueists have repeatedly demonstrated that the country possesses the talent to compete at the highest level of international snooker.

Rana Irfan's commanding 5-0 victory over three-time world champion and compatriot Muhammad Asif in the Snooker World Cup final in Muscat is another testament to Pakistan's growing stature in the sport.

From Mohammad Yousuf's historic world title in 1994 to Asif's three world championships and the emergence of younger players such as Ahsan Ramzan, Pakistan has maintained a formidable presence in international snooker.

stories.title: Hate as a governance model
summary: But beyond what Benjamin Netanyahu has done to his country, to Palestine and to the region lies the fact of Israel's existence and of its being a miniature tech superpower.
Second, less qualified BJP leaders use communal violence and virulent anti-Muslim propaganda to rise to prominence and power, Narendra Modi, Amit Shah and Yogi Adityanath being cases in point.
So, if Gadi Eisenkot in Israel and Rahul Gandhi in India were to replace the incumbents, would we witness any material change?

stories.title: External success vs internal challenges
summary: However, the country's standing as a functional democracy and vibrant economy continues to weigh heavily on investor confidence - a reality unmistakably evident in the Wave 30 survey by the Overseas Investors Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OICCI).
The survey documented a sharp drop in business confidence (overall to 23%, and among foreign investors to 27%), driven mainly by inflation, high taxation, energy costs and policy uncertainty.
Foreign investors, who showed an even steeper decline in the survey, are typically highly sensitive to governance quality, legal certainty and political stability.

stories.title: Sweden turns the page: a lesson for Pakistan's classrooms
summary: When I arrived in Gothenburg, in November 2005, as a doctoral student at Chalmers University of Technology, what struck me first was not the laboratories, impressive as they were, but the silence of the reading rooms.
So, I read with special interest the news that Sweden, once hailed as a pioneer of digital classrooms, is bringing printed textbooks back into its schools.
Sweden worried when its children dropped eleven points; many of ours cannot read at all.

stories.title: ECC raises wheat import to 2.5mt
summary: The federal government in an emergency meeting on Friday allowed import of up to 2.5 million tonnes of wheat for this year to meet shortages after delaying the decision for five months that caused a 54% spike in flour prices.

"A virtual meeting of the ECC approved, in principle, the enhancement of wheat import ceiling up to 2.5 million metric tonnes (MMT) for food year 2026-27," announced the finance ministry late Friday evening.

The ECC said that in view of the recent increase in wheat and flour prices and the need for enhanced releases from public stocks, the provinces reassessed their requirements, raising the cumulative import demand to 1.7 million tonnes.

stories.title: SPI inflation moderates to single digits
summary: According to the PBS, prices of 20 items increased during the week, nine declined, and 22 remained unchanged, showing that the overall reduction in inflation was driven by price decreases in a relatively smaller number of commodities with significant price movements.
LPG prices were 67.49% higher than a year earlier, while wheat flour recorded a 53.53% increase.
Chicken prices rose 30.10%, electricity charges for Q1 increased 29.33%, diesel 22.36% and petrol 18.34%.

stories.title: Pakistan, IFC to enhance cooperation in priority sectors
summary: Welcoming Fakhoury on his first visit to Pakistan in his current capacity, the federal minister appreciated the significant expansion of IFC's portfolio in Pakistan and its growing engagement with the government.

The discussion covered a wide range of priority areas including housing finance, public-private partnerships, privatisation of distribution companies (DISCOs), agriculture and access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
The minister highlighted the significance of IFC's support for boosting long-term housing finance, expanding access to affordable housing and facilitating financing for developers.

stories.title: Exporters embrace change to secure EU access
summary: If Pakistan loses the arrangement but retains access to the standard GSP scheme, textile exporters could face duties of around 9.6%.

Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry's former secretary general Shahid Anwar said larger exporters had made reasonable progress in meeting international requirements, particularly those supplying to established European brands.
Arif Habib Limited textile analyst Leena Abid said larger exporters generally had stronger compliance systems because of their exposure to European and German buyers.

stories.title: Pakistan Shaheens cruise into Asia Cup Rising Stars final with five-wicket win over Bangladesh ‘A’
summary: The chase was shaped by a measured third-wicket partnership between Hasan and Shahzaib Khan, who steadied the innings after Pakistan had lost both openers inside the first five overs.
Pakistan’s new-ball bowlers made early inroads, with Ali Raza dismissing both openers inside the first five overs.
Bangladesh made a cautious start and reached 41-2 after 13 overs, before Shahadat and Ankon rebuilt through patience and selective attacking shots.

stories.title: Govt increases wheat import ceiling to curb price increases
summary: ISLAMABAD: The government on Friday decided to increase the wheat import ceiling by 150 per cent to 2.5 million tonnes to check continuously rising prices of wheat and wheat flour in the market.

The decision was taken after detailed consideration of a summary submitted by the Ministry of National Food Security and Research, seeking the enhancement of the previously approved wheat import ceiling from one million tonnes to 2.5 MMT.

Last month, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar expressed concern at the rising wheat prices and directed federal and provincial governments to take all necessary measures, including increasing market supply, to bring prices under control.

stories.title: Makkah pact nations review regional security, condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
summary: A meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement’s top decision-making body on Friday reviewed the regional security situation and condemned “persistent and heinous” Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
The SPDC, which brings together the foreign and defence ministers and chiefs of defence staff of the three countries, is the alliance’s principal decision-making forum.

Managing relations with Iran will be particularly important for Pakistan, which has sought to preserve diplomatic engagement with Tehran while deepening defence cooperation with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

stories.title: President Zardari, PML-Q chief Shujaat discuss country's political situation
summary: President Asif Ali Zardari on Friday discussed the country’s political situation in a meeting with former prime minister and Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) chief Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain.
Earlier this week, Naqvi also held a meeting with Shujaat, where the debate over the creation of new provinces and devolution of powers was discussed.
In the meeting, Naqvi and Shujaat discussed the overall political situation, measures to maintain law and order, and the need to transfer power to the grassroots level.

stories.title: 3 convicted of taking woman from UK to Pakistan, forcing her into marriage: police
summary: Police in the United Kingdom said on Friday that three people had been convicted of taking a young woman from the country to Pakistan and forcing her into marriage.

Officers detained the three on Nov 7, 2024 at Birmingham Airport on suspicion of forced marriage. “We also safeguarded the woman and, after speaking to her, we established she was unaware how she had been exploited,” the police said.
Following the trial at Birmingham Crown Court, Bashir, aged 55, Bi, 55, and Aktar, 38, were convicted of the offence and will be sentenced at a later date, the statement said.

stories.title: Man buried under rubble rescued alive 2 days after building collapse in Karachi’s Baloch Colony
summary: KARACHI: A man buried under the rubble from the collapse of an under-construction six-storey building near Karachi’s Baloch Colony was rescued alive on Friday, two days after the incident occurred.
According to the statement, the chief minister directed rescue agencies and the Karachi commissioner to accelerate the ongoing rescue operation and deploy all available resources.
The building’s four owners — including Salman Tahir whose arrest the Sindh CM has ordered — its builder, architect, structural engineer and its contractors have been nominated in the FIR.

stories.title: President Zardari, Shujaat discuss national affairs, political situation
summary: President Asif Ali Zardari on Friday met former prime minister and PML-Q chief Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain, where the two leaders discussed national affairs and the prevailing political situation, according to a statement issued by the President's House.
The meeting comes amid an ongoing debate over the proposed creation of new provinces and the possibility of holding a referendum.

The debate around provinces gained momentum on July 31, when Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi called for the creation of additional provinces or administrative units, arguing that Pakistan's existing governance structure was outdated and required a comprehensive overhaul.

stories.title: SBP issues Rs200 commemorative coin to mark Mata Sahib Hasi Devi’s 200th birth anniversary
summary: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) has issued a Rs200 commemorative coin to mark the 200th birth anniversary of Pujya Mata Sahib Hasi Devi, the bank said in a statement on Friday.
The inscription “Pujya Mata Sahib Hasi Devi” appears at the top along the periphery, while the wording “200th birth anniversary” is written along the lower periphery.

Last month, Pakistan Post also issued two special commemorative postage stamps and a souvenir sheet for the 200th birth anniversary of Mata Sahib Hasi Devi to promote interfaith harmony and Sufi traditions in the region.

stories.title: Indian police say they rescued 164 foreigners trafficked for cyber fraud
summary: Indian police said they had rescued 164 foreign nationals allegedly trafficked into the country and forced to commit online fraud, in a rare case involving victims from overseas.
Fraud compounds, where international scammers lure internet users into fake romantic relationships, cryptocurrency investments and betting platforms, are common in Southeast Asia.
A United Nations report estimated this year that at least 300,000 people have been trafficked into scam compounds across Southeast Asia.

stories.title: Roads blocked, traffic congested in Karachi for 2nd consecutive day
summary: Traffic travelling from Sharea Faisal towards the airport would be diverted right from Avari traffic signal onto Fatima Jinnah Road, towards Cantt, School Road, CSD and Kala Pul, the release said.
According to updates issued by the traffic police, the road from Coast Guard towards Zainab Market and Sarwar Shaheed Road was closed to traffic at around 3:20pm in view of security.
Traffic is being sent via Avari Towers towards Fatima Jinnah Road, police said.

stories.title: Short-term inflation clocks in at 9.49pc driven by wheat flour prices
summary: ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation was recorded at 9.49 per cent year-on-year in the week ending on Nov 26, driven largely by wheat flour prices, according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Friday.

Items that recorded week-on-week price declines included tomatoes (23.92pc), onions (21.27pc), LPG (7.78pc), petrol (2.48pc), diesel (1.99pc), pulse masoor (0.68pc), sugar (0.24pc) and bananas & pulse mash (0.12pc) each.
Last week, short-term inflation was recorded at 10.41pc year-on-year, driven largely by wheat flour prices.

stories.title: Airline Norse Atlantic's Norwegian operating unit declares bankruptcy
summary: Airline Norse Atlantic’s Norwegian operating unit has declared bankruptcy, the long-haul budget carrier said on Friday, succumbing to soaring fuel costs wrought by the war on Iran.
Norse in 2021 signed long-term leases for nine Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft from Ireland-based AerCap Holdings and six Dreamliners from Singapore-based BOC Aviation Ltd.

In October, PIA signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1.

stories.title: ADB approves $468m in loans to boost water, agriculture management in KP and Punjab
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Friday approved two loans totalling $468 million to improve water and agriculture management in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab.

Valued at Rs69.893bn, the KP Resilient Irrigated Agriculture Livelihoods Development Project aims to rehabilitate the Pehur Main Canal, construct the Mulkhow Irrigation Distribution System and extend the Pehur High Level Canal.

The project aims to introduce modern spate irrigation systems, flood-protection channels, telemetry systems and centralised supervisory control and data acquisition monitoring to strengthen regional water security.

stories.title: Government reduces petrol price by Re1, keeps diesel unchanged
summary: According to a notification issued by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra), petrol will be sold at Rs312 per litre, while HSD will remain priced at Rs346 per litre.
The latest revision comes a day after the government cut petrol prices by Re1 per litre and HSD by Rs2 per litre for November 27.

Read: Govt cuts petrol by Re1, diesel by Rs2 for Nov 27 On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: PM calls for effective guidance, simplified procedures for SMEs seeking financial support
summary: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday called for better guidance for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) seeking financing from banks, enabling access to loans through simplified procedures.

Presiding over a meeting on facilitating access to credit for SMEs, the premier termed these enterprises the “backbone” of the country’s economy. “Facilitating them will boost economic activity, employment and business opportunities,” the prime minister said.

The prime minister directed the provision of effective guidance and support to SMEs to improve their access to financial resources, prepare business documentation and benefit from opportunities in the export sector.

stories.title: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform
summary: Hackers have breached the US Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a development that could jeopardise a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.
In a statement to Reuters, the Air Force said it “does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems.

Updates to applications already running on Cloud One were blocked, leaving Air Force personnel unable to apply fixes just as a new batch of serious software vulnerabilities has been disclosed across the technology industry.

stories.title: No threat to government as PM Shehbaz-CDF Munir partnership continues: Talal Chaudhry
summary: Speaking on a private television programme, Naya Pakistan, Chaudhry said the government believed in political consultations and that all major decisions were taken after bringing coalition partners on board.
Referring to Fazl's recent remarks, Chaudhry said the political resentment and anger in the JUI-F chief's statements were evident in his interviews and public appearances.
And if a government was formed in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, why was he not made its head?” Chaudhry said, describing what he believed to be the reasons behind Fazl's anger.

stories.title: Pakistan seeks deeper cooperation with IAEA on nuclear security
summary: The statement came as the 15th annual meeting of the International Network for Nuclear Security Training and Support Centres (NSSC Network), hosted by Pakistan in collaboration with the IAEA, concluded in Islamabad.
The IAEA’s unit head of the Division of Nuclear Security commended Pakistan for hosting the meeting, describing it as an important milestone in international nuclear security cooperation.
Its return to Pakistan after a decade reflected the country’s sustained engagement with the IAEA and continued contribution to international nuclear security cooperation, the statement added.

stories.title: After water and sports, India takes aim at Pakistani entertainment
summary: India's campaign to isolate Pakistan appears to be extending beyond water and sport into art and culture, with an Indian film industry organisation demanding a permanent ban on Pakistani entertainment content, including Netflix’s upcoming first Pakistani original series.

In a letter dated November 24, the association called for strict legal action and penalties against over-the-top (OTT) platforms streaming Pakistani films, dramas, songs, podcasts and other entertainment content in India.
Some have argued that if Pakistani entertainment is unwelcome in India, the streaming platform should also reconsider the availability of Indian content in Pakistan.

stories.title: FO says reports of boat carrying Pakistani migrants capsizing off Libya remain unverified
summary: It was reported earlier this week that at least 25 people from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bajaur district were feared dead or missing after a migrant boat capsized near Libya.

Previous boat tragedies In April this year, more than 80 migrants including 20 Pakistanis were reported missing after a boat carrying around 120 people capsized in the Central Mediterranean after departing from Libya.
In October last year, 18 migrants were killed when a wooden vessel capsized off the coast of Libya, while 64 people, including 12 Pakistanis, were reported missing.

stories.title: Quetta Gladiators dismiss sale rumours, reaffirm commitment to PSL
summary: Quetta Gladiators have dismissed speculation about a possible sale of the franchise or an exit from the Pakistan Super League (PSL), reaffirming their financial stability and commitment to the competition.

He also welcomed the recent direct signings of international players by PSL franchises, including New Zealand fast bowler Lockie Ferguson by Quetta Gladiators, describing the developments as evidence of the league’s growing strength.

The franchise thanked the Pakistan Cricket Board, PSL management, commercial partners and supporters for their continued backing, expressing confidence that Quetta Gladiators would remain in safe hands.

stories.title: Fleeing murder suspect crashes into elephant in Sri Lanka
summary: A Sri Lankan man suspected of fatally stabbing a woman was arrested on Friday after he crashed his scooter into a wild elephant as he attempted to escape, police said.
The 49-year-old man is accused of stabbing the woman in her home in the northern district of Anuradhapura, a police official told AFP.
However, his attempted escape ended when his scooter crashed into the elephant as it emerged from the jungle onto the road a short distance away, the official said.
